FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: The documented interface for `DetectorDiagnosis.severity` is inconsistent with the actual dataclass contract shown in the artifact. The comment says `severity: str  # "WARNING", "CRITICAL"`, but prior reviewed behaviour within the same immune boundary is already known to emit `"INFO"`. That mismatch is already listed as a known finding for comments/docs, but the stronger missed issue is that the type is an unconstrained `str`, so invalid severities are not prevented at construction time anywhere in the shown interface. This is an interface-contract weakness inside the immune boundary, not just documentation drift. Evidence: `class DetectorDiagnosis` defines `severity: str` with comment-only admissible values and no enum/validation.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `DetectorDiagnosis` dataclass uses free-form `str` for `severity`, while the immune subsystem relies on a small closed vocabulary and has already drifted beyond the documented set.  
FIX: Replace the field definition with a constrained enum and update the comment accordingly.  
<<<<
class DetectorDiagnosis:
    """Diagnosis from the detector health monitor."""
    detector: str  # "kappa", "mu", "d_decay"
    pathology: str  # human-readable description
    severity: str  # "WARNING", "CRITICAL"
    recommended_action: str  # what to do about it
    evidence: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    pathology_key: str = ""
    round_idx: int = -1
====
class DiagnosisSeverity(enum.Enum):
    INFO = "INFO"
    WARNING = "WARNING"
    CRITICAL = "CRITICAL"


class DetectorDiagnosis:
    """Diagnosis from the detector health monitor."""
    detector: str  # "kappa", "mu", "d_decay"
    pathology: str  # human-readable description
    severity: DiagnosisSeverity
    recommended_action: str  # what to do about it
    evidence: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    pathology_key: str = ""
    round_idx: int = -1
>>>>
FOLLOW: All immune code that compares or emits severities must be updated from string literals to enum values, including `has_critical` and any diagnosis constructors in `_immune.py`. Exact required follow-on replacements include:  
<<<<
return any(d.severity == "CRITICAL" for d in self._diagnoses)
====
return any(d.severity == DiagnosisSeverity.CRITICAL for d in self._diagnoses)
>>>>  
Additional downstream impact: any event/report serialization path must emit `d.severity.value` instead of the enum object. This hardens the interface and prevents further silent vocabulary drift.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

PROPOSED_FIX:
